title: Heterogeneous KV elastic-slice mapping with cross-pipeline address translation
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Implement an elastic, slabless KV slicing layer that supports heterogeneous GPU pools and staggered tensor/pipeline parallel placements. The feature must reduce peak GPU memory by redistributing KV slices dynamically across devices and pipeline stages while maintaining low-latency continuous batching. This ticket focuses on the address-translation layer, eviction hints, and spill/prefetch heuristics for cross-device requests.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end correctness for KV lookups across tensor and pipeline parallel setups with mixed-device memory capacities
Measured 20% reduction in 95th-percentile GPU memory usage on benchmark workloads with 4+ device heterogeneity
No increase in median latency > 5% under continuous-batching load compared to baseline
Automated tests for address translation, eviction, and spill backed by synthetic and replayed production traces
tasks: Design address-translation API and per-request routing tag
Prototype thin indirection table for KV pointers (device_id, slice_offset)
Integrate with continuous-batcher to annotate requests with prefetch hints
Add eviction hint generator using prefix-frequency heuristics
Implement adaptive spill-to-host with backpressure signals
Add unit and integration tests (tensor+pipeline topologies)
Benchmark on heterogeneous GPU cluster and compare with baseline
Create rollout and rollback steps for Dedicated
implementation_notes: Prefer slabless variable-length slices to avoid global compaction pauses
Use 64-bit indirection entries encoded as 'device:offset:epoch' to support in-flight reassignments
Maintain per-device mem-reservation quotas to prevent overcommit under bursty batching
Avoid cross-device synchronous barriers; use best-effort async prefetch plus short-lived rendezvous for misses
Expose tunables for prefetch window based on observed token-latency histograms
Instrument counters for cross-device miss rate, spill frequency, and prefetch efficacy
design_decisions: Choice A: slabless elastic slices over fixed slab allocation to reduce fragmentation and enable fine-grained balancing
Choice B: rendezvous-free miss handling by default to reduce tail latency; optional synchronous fallback for high-reliability customers
Choice C: predictive eviction hints derived from the continuous-batcher's request stream instead of LRU-only policies
tradeoffs: Elastic slices add indirection cost (extra memory and one pointer dereference) vs. significant reduction in fragmentation and compaction pauses
Predictive prefetch reduces misses but increases memory footprint transiently
Rendezvous-free misses can result in slightly higher background network traffic; acceptable for latency SLOs in exchange for lower p95 latency
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag 'kv.elastic_slice_mapping' on Dedicated and Private
Canary on 10% of Dedicated capacity with mixed GPU types for 48 hours
Monitor cross-device miss rate and p95 latency; rollback if miss rate increase > 2x or p95 latency increase > 10%
Progressively increase traffic to 50% then 100% while tuning prefetch window
testing_plan: Unit tests: indirection table correctness, epoch-based invalidation
Integration tests: synthetic multi-GPU topologies (2xA100 + 1xA10-style heterogeneity)
Replay tests: use two representative continuous-batching traces from production
Load tests: sustained QPS to validate spill-to-host behavior under memory pressure
Chaos tests: simulate device eviction and reassign slices while maintaining correctness
